metadata.rules_text:
- When sentiment is predominantly negative (≥15 consecutive -1.00), model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 1–3% in next 3–5 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 40–45), model overestimates; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day.
- When sentiment flips from negative to positive (e.g., 1.00 after -1.00 streak), model underreacts; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next 2–3 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true outcomes when recent history shows volatility >10% or sentiment mixed; add 1–2% upward bias to compensate for lag.
- If true outcome is significantly lower than model (e.g., >3% gap for 3+ consecutive days), model may be ignoring supply/demand shocks; re-estimate using sentiment-weighted moving average.
